The discussion of the basmalah has already come up at length in this session and in others, and we have explained that the basmalah is a verse from the Book of Allah, which Allah spoke just as He spoke the Qur'an, exalted is He. However, it is an independent verse, not counted among the verses of the surah that follows it or of the surah that precedes it. Rather, it is independent, and the surahs begin with it from Al-Fatihah to (Qul a'udhu bi-rabbi'n-nas), except for Surah Bara'ah (At-Tawbah), for it was not established from the Prophet ﷺ that he began Surah Bara'ah with the basmalah, and for this reason the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) omitted it. Yet, out of caution and fear that it might be an independent surah, they placed a separator between it and Surah Al-Anfal.

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Those who disbelieved among the People of the Book and the polytheists were not going to desist [from their disbelief] until there came to them clear evidence﴾. That is, the disbelievers among the People of the Book and the polytheists were not going to be ﴿munfakkin﴾, i.e., abandoning what they were upon of disbelief, ﴿until there came to them clear evidence﴾.

The People of the Book are the Jews and the Christians; they were so named because their scriptures remained until the Prophet ﷺ was sent, along with what was in them of alteration, distortion, and change. But they are the People of the Book. When you hear in the Qur'an "the People of the Book," who is meant? The Jews and the Christians. The Jews have the Torah, and the Christians have the Gospel. As for the polytheists, they are the worshippers of idols of every kind, from the Children of Israel and from others.

He says: these were not ﴿munfakkin﴾, i.e., abandoning what they were upon of shirk and disbelief, and separating from it, ﴿until there came to them clear evidence﴾. So what is the clear evidence?

Al-bayyinah is that by which the truth becomes clear in everything. Anything by which the truth becomes clear is called a bayyinah. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ said: "The burden of proof is upon the claimant, and the oath is upon the one who denies"[[Narrated by al-Bayhaqi (16445) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As (may Allah be pleased with them both).]]. So everything by which the truth is made manifest is a bayyinah, and it occurs in everything according to its nature. So what is the bayyinah that Allah mentioned here?

﴿Al-bayyinah⁠﴾: He said, ﴿a Messenger from Allah, reciting purified scriptures (2), in which are upright books﴾ [Al-Bayyinah 2, 3]. This Messenger is the Prophet ﷺ, Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Hashimi al-Qurashi, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him. He was described with the indefinite form ﴿a Messenger﴾ as a magnification of him, because he, peace and blessings be upon him, is worthy of being magnified with the fitting magnification, without deficiency or exaggeration.

﴿A Messenger from Allah⁠﴾ means that Allah sent him to the worlds as a bringer of good tidings and a warner. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿And We have sent you to mankind as a Messenger﴾ [An-Nisa' 79], and He said: ﴿Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant, that he may be a warner to the worlds﴾ [Al-Furqan 1]. So he is Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, sent from Allah through the medium of Jibril, peace be upon him, because Jibril is the messenger of the Lord of the worlds to His messengers, entrusted with the revelation, which he brings down upon whomever Allah wills of His servants. So who is meant by the Messenger? Muhammad. Good, who sent him? Allah; by His saying: ﴿a Messenger from Allah reciting purified scriptures﴾. Who is the intermediary between the Messenger and Allah? Jibril; because Jibril is entrusted with the revelation, which he brings down upon whomever of Allah's servants He wills.

﴿Reciting purified scriptures⁠﴾ means: he recites them for himself and for the people.

﴿Suhufan⁠﴾ is the plural of ṣaḥīfah, which is a sheet, or a tablet, or something similar on which writing is done.

﴿Muṭahharah⁠﴾ means: cleansed from shirk, from base moral qualities, and from everything that is evil, because they are pure and sanctified.

﴿Fīhā⁠﴾ means: in these scriptures ﴿kutubun qayyimah⁠﴾. ﴿Kutub⁠﴾ means: written matters that are upright. So ﴿kutub⁠﴾ is the plural of kitāb in the sense of "written," and the meaning is that in these scriptures are upright written matters which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has written. It is well known that when a person examines the Qur'an he finds it so; that is, he finds that it contains upright books, i.e., written matters. Look at what the Qur'an brought of the tawhid of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and of praising Him, glorifying Him and extolling Him; you will find it filled with that. Look at what is in the Qur'an describing the Prophet ﷺ, and describing his Companions, the Emigrants and the Helpers, and describing those who followed them in goodness. Look at what the Qur'an brought of commanding prayer, zakah, fasting, Hajj, and other noble morals; you will find that everything the Qur'an brought is upright, i.e., upright in itself, and likewise it establishes uprightness in others: ﴿in which are upright books﴾.

So Allah has informed in this verse that these disbelievers among the People of the Book and the polytheists could not desist until the clear evidence came to them. When the clear evidence came to them, did they desist from their religion, that is, from their disbelief and their shirk?

Listen to the answer. He said: ﴿And those who were given the Scripture did not differ except after the clear evidence had come to them﴾ [Al-Bayyinah 4]. That is, when the clear evidence came, did they believe? No, but they differed: some of them believed and some of them disbelieved. Among the Christians were those who believed, such as the Negus, king of Abyssinia, and among the Jews were those who believed as well, such as Abdullah ibn Salam (may Allah be pleased with him). Some believed and some disbelieved. Whoever Allah knows wants good and wants the religion for Allah, believes; he is granted success in faith, and whoever is not like that is granted success in disbelief.

Likewise, some of the polytheists believed, and how many of the polytheists of Quraysh believed! So people, before the sending of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, continued in their disbelief until the clear evidence came to them. Then, when the clear evidence came to them, what happened? They separated and differed, as Allah, exalted, said: ﴿And do not be like those who became divided and differed after the clear proofs had come to them, and those will have a great punishment﴾ [Ali 'Imran 105].

The remainder of the discussion on this surah will come, God willing.

(...) And I pray and send peace upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and upon his family, his Companions, and all who follow his guidance.

To proceed: This is the eighty-seventh of the sessions known as the "open session." This session takes place on Thursday, the twenty-second of Shawwal, in the year 1415 AH. We begin this session by completing the tafsir (explanation of the Qur'an) of Surat al-Bayyinah, and at the previous session we reached the words of Allah, blessed and exalted be He: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture (Ahl al-Kitab) and the polytheists will be in the fire of Hell, abiding eternally therein. They are the worst of creation.﴾ [Al-Bayyinah 6]

Allah, exalted be He, here makes a clear statement, emphasized by ﴿Indeed﴾, that those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists are ﴿in the fire of Hell﴾; that is, in the Fire called Jahannam. It was named Jahannam because of the depth of its bottom and its blackness, and it is derived from al-juhmah (blackness/gloom). It is also said that it is a non-Arabic word that the Arabs arabicized. Whatever the case, the word ﴿Jahannam﴾ is one of the names of the Fire, from which Allah protect us and you.

His words, ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists﴾: the word ﴿min﴾ ("among") here specifies the ambiguity of the relative pronoun (al-ism al-mawsul) in His words ﴿those who disbelieved﴾. Accordingly, this implies that the People of the Scripture are disbelievers, namely the Jews and the Christians. The matter is so, for the Jews and the Christians are disbelievers because they did not believe in the Messenger of Allah, Muhammad (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). Even if they say that they believe in Allah and the Last Day, and pray for mercy upon their dead, and similar expressions by which they seek closeness, they are liars. For if they truly believed in Allah and the Last Day, they would have believed in Muhammad (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and indeed they would have believed in their own messengers. This is because the Prophet (ﷺ) has been described in the Torah and the Gospel, as Allah, blessed and exalted be He, said in Surat al-A'raf: ﴿Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered prophet, whom they find written in what they have of the Torah and the Gospel, who enjoins upon them what is good and forbids them from what is wrong, and makes lawful for them the good things and prohibits for them the evil things﴾ [Al-A'raf 157]. Moreover, Jesus (ﷺ) said to the Children of Israel: ﴿O Children of Israel, indeed I am the messenger of Allah to you, confirming what came before me of the Torah and bringing good tidings of a messenger who will come after me, whose name is Ahmad﴾ [As-Saf 6]. So when this Messenger whom Jesus had given good tidings of came with clear proofs, they said: "This is evident magic," and they denied him and did not follow him, except for a small group from the Jews and the Christians who believed in Muhammad (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and followed him.

﴿They are the worst of creation﴾: ﴿the worst of creation (al-bariyyah)﴾ means the worst of the creatures, because al-bariyyah is the creation. Accordingly, the disbelievers among the children of Adam, from the Jews, the Christians, and the polytheists, are the worst of al-bariyyah, the worst of all creatures. Allah has fully explained this in His words: ﴿Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are those who disbelieve, and they will not believe﴾ [Al-Anfal 55], and He, exalted be He, said: ﴿Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are the deaf and the mute who do not reason. And if Allah had known any good in them, He would have made them hear. And even if He had made them hear, they would have turned away while they were refusing﴾ [Al-Anfal 22–23]. Thus these disbelievers among the Jews, the Christians, and the polytheists are the worst of creation in the sight of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. And since they are the worst of creation, we should expect from them nothing but every evil, for evil springs forth from the wicked, and it is never possible for us to think well of them. We may trust some of the truthful among them, as the Prophet (ﷺ) trusted the polytheist Abd Allah ibn Uraykit when he hired him to guide him on the way of the migration (hijrah). But most of them, and the majority, cannot be trusted, because they are evil.

The Quran is a book of repeated themes (mathani), in which meanings are stated together with their opposites. It brings up the people of the Fire and the people of Paradise, the verses of warning and the verses of glad tidings, and so on, so that a person may travel to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, between fear and hope, and so that he does not grow weary. Variety in styles and subjects undoubtedly gives the soul strength and drive, unlike a discourse that proceeds in one uniform tone, where a person may grow weary and his soul will not stir.

﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds—it is they who are the best of creation.﴾ Those who believe and do righteous deeds are the best of Allah's creation, the Mighty and Majestic, and they are of four ranks, which Allah explained in His saying: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger—those are with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor from among the prophets, the steadfast in truth (al-siddiqin), the martyrs, and the righteous.﴾ These four ranks are the ranks of the believers. The highest of them is the rank of prophethood, and the highest rank within prophethood is the rank of messengership. Then, after prophethood, comes the rank of siddiqiyyah (truthfulness of the highest degree), and at the head of the siddiqin is Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him. As for the martyrs (shuhada'), it has been said that they are the people of knowledge, and it has been said that they are those who were killed in the way of Allah. The verse can bear both meanings together without contradiction, and the proper course for an exegete of the Quran, when a verse can bear two meanings without contradiction, is to take it as bearing both meanings. So the martyrs are the people of knowledge and those who were killed in the way of Allah, and all of them have a high rank above all who follow the messengers, except the siddiqin. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿and the righteous﴾, and they are the lowest of the ranks. So those who believe and do righteous deeds, across their different ranks, are the best of creation; that is, the best of what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has created of creatures.

Then He explained their reward, saying: ﴿Their reward with their Lord is Gardens of Eden beneath which rivers flow﴾ [al-Bayyinah 8]. Here Allah placed praise of the believers who did righteous deeds before mention of their reward, because Allah's praise of them is of greater rank and higher virtue. For this reason He mentioned it before the reward, which is their recompense on the Day of Resurrection.

﴿Their reward with their Lord is Gardens of Eden beneath which rivers flow﴾. ﴿Gardens﴾ is in the plural because of the variety of their kinds, for the Prophet (ﷺ) said that the gardens are: "Two gardens of gold, their vessels and everything in them, and two gardens of silver, their vessels and everything in them"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4878) and Muslim (180 / 296), from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari (may Allah be pleased with him), but with the mention of silver placed before gold.]]. To this points the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And for whoever fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens﴾ [ar-Rahman 46], then He described the attributes of these two gardens, then said: ﴿And besides them are two gardens﴾ [ar-Rahman 62]. Thus they have gardens.

The gardens that Allah mentioned as a reward for the believers who did righteous deeds are great abodes that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has prepared for the righteous believers. ﴿In them is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived﴾[[Recorded by Muslim (2825 / 5) from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi (may Allah be pleased with him).]]. A person in this world can never truly imagine the bliss of the Hereafter, because it is higher and greater than what we imagine. Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: "There is nothing in Paradise of what is in this world except the names"[[Recorded by Hannad in al-Zuhd (3) from him, and its wording: "There is nothing in Paradise of what is in this world except the names."]]. However, the realities differ greatly.

He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Gardens of Eden﴾. ʿAdn means dwelling in a place and not departing from it. Among the completeness of the bliss of the people of Paradise is that each of them does not seek a change from the bliss he is in, because he does not see anyone more perfect than himself, and he does not feel in his heart any diminishment compared to one who is higher and more perfect. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿They will not desire any change from them﴾ [al-Kahf 108], meaning they do not seek a change from what they are in, because Allah has made them content with what He gave them, so they find no one with more complete bliss than theirs. For this reason Allah named these gardens "Gardens of Eden." I ask Allah to make me and you among its people.

﴿beneath which rivers flow﴾. ﴿Beneath them﴾: the scholars said, beneath their palaces and trees, otherwise the rivers are on its surface and not lower; rather they are beneath these palaces and trees. The rivers that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned here in general terms, He explained in Surah Muhammad, saying: ﴿The description of the Garden promised to the righteous: in it are rivers of water unchanging, and rivers of milk whose taste does not change, and rivers of wine, delicious to drinkers, and rivers of purified honey﴾ [Muhammad 15]. These are the rivers. It has also been reported in traditions describing these rivers that "they flow without trenches and without ditches"[[Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilya (6 / 205) reported from Anas ibn Malik who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Perhaps you think that the rivers of Paradise are a trench in the earth. No, by Allah, they flow over the surface of the earth, their banks are tents of pearls, and their clay is musk, the pungent musk." I said: O Messenger of Allah, what is al-Adhfar? He said: "That which has no admixture with it." It was also reported by Ibn Abi al-Dunya in Sifat al-Jannah (69) from Anas as a statement of his own (mawquf).]]. This means that the river flows on the surface of the earth, turning wherever a person directs it, and it needs no digging of trenches nor the construction of a ditch to prevent the water from flowing right and left. On this Ibn al-Qayyim (may Allah have mercy on him) said in his Nuniyya:

Its rivers flow without a trench,
Glory be to the One who keeps them from overflowing.

﴿Abiding therein forever﴾ [al-Bayyinah 8]: meaning remaining there forever; they do not die, nor fall ill, nor despair, nor suffer, nor grieve, and no weariness touches them therein. They are in the most complete bliss always and forever, for eternity without end. O Allah, make us among them.

﴿Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him﴾ [al-Bayyinah 8]. This is the most complete bliss: that Allah is pleased with them, so He causes His pleasure to descend upon them, and He never becomes displeased with them after that. Indeed, they look upon Allah, blessed and exalted, with their eyes as they see the moon on the night of the full moon, having no doubt about it and no difficulty in it, and not being crowded in seeing Him[[Recorded by al-Bukhari (554) and Muslim (633 / 211) from Jarir ibn 'Abd Allah al-Bajali (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: We were sitting with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he looked at the moon on the night of the full moon and said: "Indeed, you will see your Lord just as you see this moon, you will not be crowded in seeing Him. So if you are able not to be overcome in a prayer before the rising of the sun and before its setting," meaning the 'Asr and Fajr prayers. Then Jarir recited: ﴿And glorify the praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting﴾ [Ta-Ha: 130].]]; that is, they do not press upon one another to see Him, but each person sees Him in his place, according to what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wills.

Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿That is for whoever fears his Lord﴾ [al-Bayyinah 8]: that reward is for whoever fears Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Khashya (fear) is the fear of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, joined with awe and reverence, and it does not arise except from one who knows Allah, as He, Exalted, said: ﴿Only those among His servants who have knowledge fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Almighty, Oft-Forgiving﴾ [Fatir 28]. With this this great surah is complete, and what was made possible for us of discussion on its tafsir is complete. We ask Allah to make us all among those who recite the Book of Allah with its due recitation. Indeed, He is over all things Competent.
